content:
Hi! I just opened a small mathlib PR:
https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/42110

It adds Path.length for paths in a PseudoEMetricSpace, defined via variation, together with:

  • Path.edist_le_length
  • Path.length_refl
  • Path.length_symm
  • Path.length_trans

This is intended as a first step toward a broader theory of rectifiable paths.
I’d be very happy for any comments or review suggestions. Thanks!
Eventually I will prove that in a strict convex space, every shortest path between two points is the straight line segment up to monotonic reparametrisation.
OOps, one simp fail in checks, it was fine on my computer. I will correct it later.
Ok it is fixed now. Hi everyone, welcome to review it!

I think this overlaps with the path_metric.lean file in this old mathlib3 PR. The proofs there might inspire you to golf your proofs. Part of that PR is ported to #31766, but not the path_metric file, and some review comments remain to be addressed. You might consider how to best integrate your PR with #31766.

Thanks, this is very helpful. I took a closer look at #31766, and I really like it — it is clearly more general, and in many ways it feels like the better long-term design for mathlib. In particular, I like that many of the early results are developed in a more general setting rather than only for paths.

My hesitation is mainly practical: #31766 is quite old (from 2023), and if I am reading the history correctly, the last commit there was in December 2025. So I am a bit worried that if I tie this small PR too closely to that development, it may get stuck for a long time as well.

Given that, what do you think is the best thing for me to do here? Would you recommend that I keep this PR as a small independent path-specific result, or would it be better to close it and instead try to contribute in the direction of #31766? I’d be very happy to follow whichever direction seems more appropriate.
